name: Universal Modder
tagline: A game-modding toolkit for AI agents - tell Claude Code what you want changed in a game, and it does the modding for you.
sentence: Ask Claude Code to add a new weapon to Terraria or build a civilization for Age of Empires 2 - Universal Modder gives it the playbooks and tools to mod 12 game engines.

visual.alt: A pipeline diagram showing two routes: a 3D route (concept to 3D model to render) and a 2D route (image to sprite cutout to sprite fit to in-game), with labeled steps at each stage.
visual.caption: The modding pipeline: from a concept to an in-game asset, through 3D modeling or 2D sprite creation.

board.say: You want to mod a game - add a weapon, a character, a map - but learning each engine's modding tools takes hours, and every game works differently.
board.eg: You want to add a custom sword to Terraria, but that means learning tModLoader, setting up the project structure, writing the item code and compiling a mod.

board.say: You ask Claude Code to mod the game, or run the `um` command yourself.
board.eg: `um mod terraria 'Add a legendary crystal sword that shoots beams'` - the agent reads Terraria's modding playbook and starts building.

board.say: A description of what you want - a weapon, a character, a civilization, a map - and which game it's for.
board.eg: A new civilization for Age of Empires 2, a weapons pack for Terraria, or a vehicle mod for GTA V.

board.say: It gives your AI agent step-by-step playbooks for 12 game engines, handles asset creation and compiles a working mod.
steps: The agent reads the engine playbook (Terraria, AoE2, GTA V, Minecraft, Unity, Unreal and more) to learn that engine's modding workflow
It generates the assets (sprites, 3D models, textures) using the 2D or 3D pipeline
It writes the mod code, sets up the project structure and compiles the mod for the target engine
board.eg: The README's Terraria example: describe a weapon, and the agent generates the sprite, writes the item code, and produces a loadable tModLoader mod.

board.say: A working game mod, ready to load into your game.

outputs.eg: A tModLoader mod for Terraria with a custom weapon, ready to drop into your mods folder
Sprites, 3D models or textures created through the modding pipeline
The full project structure, so you can open it in the engine's modding tools and keep editing

before: Modding a game means learning that engine's modding tools, project structure and asset format - a different setup for every game.
Creating game assets (sprites, models, textures) for a mod means learning a 3D tool or pixel editor on top of the modding tools.
after: Describe what you want and which game - the AI agent handles the engine-specific workflow, asset creation and compilation.
12 engine playbooks in one toolkit: mod Terraria, AoE2, GTA V, Minecraft, Unity, Unreal and more with the same tool.
uses_note: Universal Modder is 9 days old. Named real-world use outside the project's own demos is still very early.

pulse.gain: +4.1K stars this week. 5.8K total in 9 days.

steps: [Read the Universal Modder README](https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder) to see which game engines are supported and what the `um` command does.
Install Universal Modder in Claude Code and pick a game you own. Ask Claude Code to create a simple mod (a new item or character).
Load the generated mod into your game and test it. Check the project files to see the full structure the agent created.

footprint.disk: No data found for install size. It is a set of skills, tools and playbooks that Claude Code uses - not a standalone application.
footprint.memory: No data found. Runs through Claude Code, so resource use depends on the modding task and the game engine's own tools.
footprint.runs_on: Wherever Claude Code runs (Mac, Windows, Linux). Each game engine has its own platform requirements.

best_for: You want to mod games but don't want to learn each engine's modding tools - describe what you want and let the AI handle the details
You play multiple moddable games and want one toolkit that covers Terraria, AoE2, GTA V, Minecraft and more
skip_if: You are an experienced modder who already knows your engine's tools - Universal Modder adds a layer of AI abstraction you may not need
You want to mod a game not in the 12 supported engines - you'd need to write your own playbook

alternatives.name: Nexus Mods
alternatives.line: The largest mod-sharing site. Download finished mods from other creators instead of building your own.

alternatives.name: Manual modding with engine tools
alternatives.line: Each engine's official modding toolkit (tModLoader for Terraria, Creation Kit for Skyrim). More control, but you learn each one separately.

watch: **9 days old and early.** The playbooks and asset pipelines are new. Expect rough edges, especially on less-tested engines.
**Quality depends on the AI agent.** The mod's code and assets are generated by Claude Code. Complex mods may need manual editing.
**You need the game and its modding tools installed.** Universal Modder drives the modding workflow but doesn't replace the game's own mod loader or compiler.
**Only 125 commits so far.** The project is small. Playbook coverage and asset-pipeline quality will improve - or stall - depending on the maintainer.
